claims: C1: without the recommended formatting, untrusted input might contain malicious instructions (prompt injection)
C2: without the recommended formatting, it can be extremely difficult for the assistant to distinguish such malicious instructions from the developer's instructions

concepts.name: untrusted_input
concepts.gloss: input data that is not trusted by the developer and is placed in a message or block without the recommended formatting
concepts.inference: the node's claim speaks of 'untrusted input' and 'without this formatting'; the class of such input is presupposed by the source text

concepts.name: malicious_instruction
concepts.gloss: a set of instructions embedded in the untrusted input that is malicious, i.e. intended to make the assistant act against the developer's or user's interests
concepts.inference: the source text names 'malicious instructions' and equates them with 'prompt injection'; the class is presupposed by the source text

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction issued at the developer authority level, as defined by the document-wide shared signature
concepts.inference: the source text refers to 'the developer's instructions'; the meaning is the one the shared-name signature assigns

concepts.name: hard_to_distinguish
concepts.gloss: the assistant cannot reliably tell whether instruction I is a developer instruction or a malicious instruction embedded in untrusted input U
concepts.inference: the source text says it is 'extremely difficult' to distinguish them; the relation between an instruction and the input it comes from is presupposed

concepts.name: unformatted_input
concepts.gloss: input that is placed in a message or block without the recommended formatting (untrusted_text block, YAML, JSON, or XML)
concepts.inference: the source text contrasts 'without this formatting' with the recommended formats; the class is presupposed by the source text

concepts.name: contains_instruction
concepts.gloss: input I contains instruction X as part of its content
concepts.inference: the source text says the untrusted input 'might contain' malicious instructions; the containment relation is presupposed

ontology.gloss: an instruction contained in an unformatted untrusted input is a malicious instruction (prompt injection)
when an unformatted untrusted input contains an instruction, it is extremely difficult for the assistant to distinguish that instruction from a developer instruction
